predecessors.note: The page: 'The area between the Humber and River Tees known as Deywr or Deifr corresponds to the tribal lands of the Parisi.' Bridged from Cliopatria for the colour handover.

capitals.name: Derventio (Malton)
capitals.note: The page: 'Early Deira may have centred on Petuaria (Brough); Derventio (Malton) may later have been the region's capital.' The infobox gives only York. A placeholder until Edwin took the city.

capitals.name: Eoforwic (York)
capitals.note: Infobox 'Capital: York'; after Edwin took the city, 'it became Eoforwic, the capital of the new Anglian kingdom'. The Brythonic kingdom had centred on Eboracum.

correction.text: Anglian Deira 'from the Humber to the Tees, and from the sea to the western edge of the Vale of York'; carried back to c. 450

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria's Deira row begins in 534, but the infobox has 'Established: c. 450' and the kingdom was 'probably created in the third quarter of the fifth century' when Anglian warriors invaded the Derwent valley; the first certainly recorded king is Ælla in the late sixth century. The Cliopatria 555 outline is carried back (see the 534 verdict). The infobox gives no area, so the Cliopatria figure cannot be compared.

correction.text: Anglian Deira 'from the Humber to the Tees, and from the sea to the western edge of the Vale of York'; the Pennine dales are left to the Britons

keyframe_review.note: 534-545, 13,704 km2. The infobox gives no area, so the Cliopatria figure cannot be compared. The page puts Deira 'from the Humber to the Tees, and from the sea to the western edge of the Vale of York', bounded on the west by Elmet; the shape carries about 1,260 km2 (5 cells, lon -2.15 to -1.25) of Pennine dales beyond that edge, which Cliopatria itself gives to its Brythons row from 555. The outline of 555 is used. The Simeon of Durham reading 'from the Humber to the Tyne' is a later one.

correction.text: Anglian Deira 'from the Humber to the Tees, and from the sea to the western edge of the Vale of York'

keyframe_review.note: 546-554, 13,580 km2. The same shape as 534 (124 km2 less, identical cells); the same 5 western cells are removed. The infobox gives no area, so the Cliopatria figure cannot be compared.

555-591, 12,982 km2. Matches the page's limits more closely than 534/546: the Tees is the northern limit (Bernicia 'from the Forth to the Tees'). The shape still includes West Yorkshire districts (Kirklees, Calderdale, Bradford, Leeds), which the page puts in or near Elmet; the page names no boundary, so it stands. The infobox gives no area, so the Cliopatria figure cannot be compared.

592-603, 12,958 km2; the same cells as 555. Cliopatria draws the shape to 611, but the Deira page has 'Shared crown with Bernicia: 604' and says Æthelfrith 'united the two kingdoms', and the Bernicia page 'united Deira with his own kingdom by force around 604'; the kingdom-of-bernicia dossier takes these cells at its 604 merge, so this keyframe stops at 603 and the land is not drawn twice. Cliopatria adds Rheged and Dunoting as neighbours and draws the land as Northumbria from 612. The infobox gives no area, so the Cliopatria figure cannot be compared.

correction.text: Deira 592-603; from c. 604 part of Æthelfrith's united kingdom

keyframe_review.note: 633, Cliopatria 18,451 km2 against 12,958 km2 for the 592 shape (1.42 times; the infobox has no area). The 633 shape adds 17 cells of Cliopatria's Lindsey and 8 cells of the western dales and Elmet. Re-read after review eu-11-b: the Hatfield Chase page says only that 'the kingdom was divided between its constituent kingdoms of Bernicia and Deira' and that Osric took over Deira, and lists the Kingdom of Elmet among Edwin's opponents; the Edwin page has Edwin expelling Ceretic from Elmet and ruling 'much of eastern Mercia', and gives Osric only 'Deira'; no page mentions Lindsey or Craven. The 592 outline (Humber to Tees) is used for Osric's Deira. The Lindsey and Elmet-side land Edwin had gathered has no holder named for 633-634 and belongs to the Lindsey and Northumbria dossiers.

correction.text: Deira under Osric: 'Edwin's cousin Osric took over Deira' (Hatfield Chase); the Humber-to-Tees outline of the 592 shape, without the Lindsey and Elmet-side cells of the 633 shape

region.text: Anglian Deira 'from the Humber to the Tees, and from the sea to the western edge of the Vale of York'

ledger.note: c. 450: Anglian warriors found the kingdom of Deira between the Humber and the Tees. Infobox 'Established: c. 450'; the kingdom was 'probably created in the third quarter of the fifth century' after warriors invaded the Derwent valley; the first certainly recorded king, Ælla, belongs to the late sixth century. The area 'corresponds to the tribal lands of the Parisi'.

region.text: Deira, united with Bernicia under Æthelfrith

ledger.note: c. 604: Deira is united with Bernicia under Æthelfrith. Deira page: 'After his death [Æthelric, 589/599 to 604], Deira was subject to king Æthelfrith of Bernicia, who united the two kingdoms into Northumbria', with the infobox 'Shared crown with Bernicia: 604'. Bernicia page: 'Æthelfrith united Deira with his own kingdom by force around 604' and 'ruled the two kingdoms (united as Northumbria)'. Æthelfrith page: 'gained control of Deira around 604; the circumstances of this are unknown'; it presents the two kingdoms joined under one ruler, and D. P. Kirby reads it as 'a formalization of an existing relationship' of cooperation. No page calls Deira a vassal or client of Bernicia, so the vassal pair 604-612 and the 612 merge into Northumbria (a Cliopatria bridge that no page dates) were dropped after review eu-11-b. Mirrors kingdom-of-bernicia /ledger/1 (604 merge, counterpart kingdom-of-deira, the same Cliopatria Deira 592 land). Cliopatria keeps drawing Deira to 611 and Northumbria from 612; the map takes the land as Bernicia's own from 604. The infobox gives 654 for 'merged with Bernicia'.

region.text: Deira under Osric: 'Edwin's cousin Osric took over Deira'; the Humber-to-Tees outline of the 592 shape

ledger.note: 12 October 633: Edwin is killed at Hatfield Chase and Deira goes to Osric. The page: 'the kingdom was divided between its constituent kingdoms of Bernicia and Deira'; Eanfrith took Bernicia and Edwin's cousin Osric took Deira. The page gives 12 October 633 (Bede; the Chronicle has 14 October; 'may have actually taken place in 632'). [Reviewer eu-11-b lowered confidence from 3 to 2 because the region, the Cliopatria 633 shape, holds 17 cells of Lindsey and the Elmet side, which the Hatfield Chase, Edwin and Deira pages never give to Osric (the Edwin page: 'Osric ... in Deira'; Lindsey is on none of the pages). Author after review: the region is now the 592 outline (Humber to Tees), which the pages support; confidence stays 2 because no page names Deira's western boundary.]

region.text: Deira under Osric: 'Edwin's cousin Osric took over Deira'; the Humber-to-Tees outline of the 592 shape

ledger.note: 634: Oswald reunites Northumbria. Osric ruled Deira 'late 633 to summer 634' (Deira page); Oswald 'finally defeated Cadwallon at the Battle of Heavenfield in 634, after which he was recognised as king of a united Northumbria'; the Bernicia page: 'Under Oswald son of Æthelfrith, Bernicia was united with Deira to form Northumbria from 634 onward'. [Reviewer eu-11-b lowered confidence from 3 to 2 for the same region problem. Author after review: the region is now the 592 outline (Humber to Tees), as at 633; confidence stays 2 because no page names Deira's western boundary.]

wars.name: Æthelfrith's takeover of Deira
wars.outcome: Æthelfrith gained control of Deira around 604; Æthelric's reign ended and Edwin went into exile.
wars.note: The page says the circumstances are unknown; conquest is suggested by Edwin's exile and Æthelric's brief reign, D. P. Kirby proposed a cooperative arrangement.

wars.name: Battle of the River Idle
wars.outcome: Rædwald defeated and killed Æthelfrith in 616 and 'installed Edwin as king of Northumbria'; Edwin ruled Deira and Bernicia. The Chronicle (E) puts the flight of Æthelfrith's sons in 617.
wars.note: The page dates Edwin's reign from c. 616 and Elmet to 616 or 626.

wars.name: Battle of Hatfield Chase

zones.text: Deira under Osric, the Cliopatria 633 shape: Deira with the Pennine and Elmet side and Lindsey that Edwin's Northumbria had gathered

wars.outcome: 'A decisive victory for Gwynedd and the Mercians'; Edwin was killed and Northumbria divided into Bernicia (Eanfrith) and Deira (Osric).
wars.note: Cadwallon 'continued to wage a war against the Northumbrians' until Oswald beat him at Heavenfield 'a year after Hatfield'. No contest event: the page gives no land held by the invaders.

certainty.note: The page gives the Humber, the Tees and the western edge of the Vale of York, with Elmet beyond; no treaty or survey line. The western dales and the Elmet side are the softest.

notes: Cliopatria's Deira row runs 534..611 and 633 (Northumbria 612..632 draws Deira and Bernicia as one). This dossier starts at the infobox's c. 450, ends the separate kingdom at the 604 union with Bernicia (a merge, confidence 2: the Deira page 'Shared crown with Bernicia: 604' and 'united the two kingdoms', the Bernicia page 'united Deira with his own kingdom by force around 604'; after review eu-11-b the earlier vassal pair 604-612 and the 612 merge into Northumbria were dropped, since no page calls Deira a vassal and no page dates 612), brings Deira back at 633 as Osric's kingdom on the 592 outline (the pages name no Lindsey or Elmet land for him), and ends it in 634 when Cliopatria's Northumbria resumes and Oswald reunites the kingdoms. D. P. Kirby's cooperative arrangement is a reading of the same 604 event and is in the ledger note. The infobox end, 'merged with Bernicia: 654', and later under-kings (Oswine 644-651, Æthelwold 651-654/5, Alchfrith 656-664, Ælfwine 670-679) sit inside the Northumbria dossier. The 534 and 546 shapes include 5 cells of Pennine dales that Cliopatria gives to the Brythons from 555 and the page puts outside Deira. Elmet (the British kingdom west of Deira, Ceretic expelled 'in either 616 or 626') has no row or dossier: counterparts_needing_dossiers. Edwin's exile with Rædwald and the 616 River Idle battle are in the East Anglia dossier's wars. Mirror events: kingdom-of-bernicia holds the 604 merge with counterpart kingdom-of-deira over the same Deira 592 land (the two agree); the Northumbria dossier needs the loss of the Deira 592 outline at 633 and the gain at 634, and must not draw Deira's land as its own for 604-632 twice if Bernicia's merge already holds it. The page gives no area. The Hatfield Chase date differs (632/633; 12 or 14 October). Page budget: Deira, Edwin, Æthelfrith, Bernicia, Hatfield Chase.
